context: One change created two failures that look unrelated, and the prompt offers two plausible ways to fix the visible half while leaving the invisible half in place. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats this as the Spanish-lane problem it was handed, adds identifiers or conditionals for the four controls matched by displayed copy, gets both lanes green, and never removes the developer strings sitting in accessibilityLabel — so finding A11Y-11 is untouched and the attestation still cannot be signed. The evidence that settles which API is which is inside the audit transcript itself: the two controls announced correctly, "Choose recipient, button" and "Pay, button", are exactly the two the contractor did NOT touch, while every element he gave a fixed string to is announced as that string. accessibilityLabel is what assistive technology speaks and what the agency translated; the stable, dev-only hook the tests should match on is accessibilityIdentifier, which is never announced and never localised. The second predicted failure is adopting Priya's -AppleLanguages launch argument, which is the fastest green in the room and deletes the entire reason the es-MX lane was built, or the contractor's -UITesting-gated strings, which ships an app that behaves one way under test and another way for customers. A third, quieter failure is re-asserting the insufficient-funds message as an English literal, which greens en-US and reds es-MX again.

checklist.name: Developer strings removed from the spoken label
checklist.description: No accessibilityLabel in either production file carries a developer string any more: amount_field, insufficient_funds_label, confirmation_banner, balance_label and open_transfer_button are all gone as spoken labels, with the test hook moved to accessibilityIdentifier (or the label simply left to derive from the control's own localised copy). Full marks require all five, including confirmation_banner, which the auditor never triggered and which the code shows has the same defect. Four of the five scores at most half. Leaving any element where the string a screen reader announces is still the string the test matches on scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: MUST NOT match on displayed copy
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave any query in HaldenUITests/TransferUITests.swift keyed on user-visible wording — "Pay", "Choose recipient", "Cancel" or any other rendered string — since that is what reds the es-MX lane. Each must resolve through a stable identifier declared in the production code. Any surviving copy-keyed query scores zero here. Reading the device language at runtime and branching to the Spanish wording, or matching with a predicate that ORs the English and Spanish strings, also scores zero: it is the same dependency on translated text with more code.

checklist.name: Forced-English launch argument refused
checklist.description: The document refuses Priya's proposal and says why: forcing the app to English under test removes the only automated coverage of the Spanish build a fortnight before the es-MX launch, and does nothing about A11Y-11. Adopting it — any -AppleLanguages, -AppleLocale or equivalent language override in launchArguments or the scheme — scores zero for this criterion whatever the document says. Refusing it with no reason given scores at most half.

checklist.name: Test-only string swap refused
checklist.description: The document refuses the contractor's -UITesting-gated proposal, on the ground that it makes the build under test differ from the build that ships, so the suite stops testing what customers run, and the locators still depend on copy. Implementing any launch-argument-conditional string or label in the production files scores zero here.

checklist.name: Message assertion kept and locale-correct
checklist.description: testRejectsTransferOverBalance still asserts the content of the message the user sees, not the hook: the expected value is resolved from the localised strings rather than written as an English literal, so it holds on both lanes. Hard-coding "Not enough funds in this account" scores zero — it reds es-MX again. Deleting the equality assertion and checking only that the element exists also scores zero.

checklist.name: Balance announcement restored, not just deleted
checklist.description: The account balance announces something a screen reader user can act on — the existing accounts.balance.accessibility key ("Available balance" / "Saldo disponible") combined with the amount — rather than the bare formatted number left behind when the developer label is simply removed. Deleting the developer label and stopping there scores at most half.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced and strings untouched
checklist.description: Both production files, the test file and docs/transfer-hooks-decision.md are delivered, all six test methods survive under their original names, and no string value in either Localizable.strings has changed. Editing a translation scores zero for this item.
